tools.title: Find Elements by Category
tools.description: Discover existing host Rooms and Spaces by category, name and level before choosing a RoomTag or SpaceTag. Omit viewId and sheetNumber for document-wide discovery: spatial elements hidden in a view are absent from its visible inventory, so that absence does not prove the host lacks a corresponding room or space. Match exact identity, level and placement before using a host space for an annotation of a linked room. Count placed elements by category and group returned family and type only when itemsComplete is true. A truncated result is not a complete inventory. Selector helper: find element ids by scope (viewId OR sheetNumber) and filters. Supports sheet-region targeting, visible-text search, and bounded document discovery across instance name, family, type, category, and Mark. identityTerms uses exact phrase or at-least-half meaningful-token overlap and returns the matched evidence. physicalElementsOnly excludes view-owned/non-model artifacts; topLevelInstancesOnly excludes nested children. expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters performs a second, category-grounded scan for delimiter-bounded phrase acronyms in string parameters and returns the exact parameter evidence; it never expands without a first-pass physical identity seed. includeGeometry adds each physical result's world-space location, axis-aligned bounding box, orientation, type, level, host, and location-curve length/straightness. Agent projections expose routeCurveCandidates for bounded duct/pipe edit discovery; connector topology must still be verified before mutation. Body: {viewId?,sheetNumber?,includeSheetElements?,includeViewportElements?,sheetRegions?:[{minU,minV,maxU,maxV}],regionPaddingFt?,category?,categories?,typeNameContains?,familyNameContains?,nameContains?,markContains?,textContains?,identityTerms?:string[],physicalElementsOnly?,topLevelInstancesOnly?,expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters?,includeGeometry?,limit?}.
tools.example: find physical air-terminal instances with world geometry anywhere in this project
notes: Scope precedence: if viewId is provided it is used; otherwise sheetNumber scopes to views placed on that sheet (viewports).
For redline workflows, provide sheetRegions (sheet UV boxes) to return only elements overlapping mapped markup areas.
Categories are BuiltInCategory tokens like OST_Doors, OST_TitleBlocks, OST_GenericModel.

For ordinary whole-document object discovery, identityTerms searches instance name, family, type, category, and Mark while preserving matched-term/field evidence; combine physicalElementsOnly and topLevelInstancesOnly to exclude schedules, legends, annotations, and nested child components.

expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters is seed-gated: only categories with a physical first-pass identity match are scanned for delimiter-bounded phrase acronyms in string parameters, and exact parameter-name/value evidence is returned.

includeGeometry=true returns model/world coordinates, transformed axis-aligned bounding boxes, FamilyInstance facing/hand orientation, and type/level/host ids for bounded project-wide spatial analysis without requiring a visible view export.

tools.title: Update Parameter By Query
tools.description: Find elements by category/text filters, inspect one parameter, and set a new value only when blank or matching the query criteria. Supports preview/apply reporting for repetitive parameter-fill tasks. Body: {category?,categories?,matchStartsWith?,matchContains?,matchParameterNames?,familyNameContains?,typeNameContains?,parameterName,value,onlyWhenBlank?,dryRun?,apply?,confirm?,limit?}.

tools.title: Locate Elements
tools.description: Spatial locator helper for filtering elements by category, level, room, and proximity. It also reports nested-parent evidence. Set spatialResolution=geometry or geometry_with_nearest to batch-resolve each result against host Rooms, host Spaces, and transformed linked architectural Rooms with explicit resolved/ambiguous/unresolved status and provenance. spatialVerticalScope=volume (default) requires strict 3D containment. spatialVerticalScope=same_level requires geometry, ignores native association-only evidence, and uses the target's factual level plus 2D room footprint for above-ceiling/plenum devices; it never searches other levels. If same_level is paired with association, the handler promotes the request to geometry. An explicit phase or active-view phase is strict. When neither exists, the read-only fallback first checks mapped phases where the target exists. If those phases contain no factual room footprint, it may use all mapped phase variants only when the same-level containing variants agree on one numbered spatial identity; phaseFallbackUsed reports that provenance. Unknown mappings, conflicting identities, and boundary-only evidence fail closed. Unavailable link/transform/element-location/level evidence also fails closed. Body: {elementIds?,categories?,levelNames?,roomNumber?,roomNameContains?,nearElementId?,maxDistanceFt?,limit?,spatialResolution?:association|geometry|geometry_with_nearest,spatialVerticalScope?:volume|same_level,spatialKindPreference?:auto|room|space|all,includeHostRooms?,includeHostSpaces?,includeLinkedRooms?,linkedModelNameContains?,phaseId?,phaseName?,nearestCandidateLimit?}.
tools.example: find the room number for each selected device
notes: association preserves the fast existing FamilyInstance Room/Space lookup. geometry adds phase-aware Room/Space containment against host and transformed linked spatial elements. geometry_with_nearest also returns ranked candidates for unresolved elements. spatialVerticalScope=volume is the strict 3D default; same_level ignores association-only evidence, requires factual same-level 2D footprints for above-ceiling/plenum devices, and never broadens to another level. Pairing same_level with association promotes the request to geometry.

Geometry mode uses an explicit phase or the active-view phase when available. If neither exists, it first evaluates mapped phases where the target exists. When those phases contain no footprint, it may evaluate all mapped phase variants, but resolves only when the containing variants agree on one numbered identity; phaseFallbackUsed reports that provenance and disagreements remain ambiguous. Unloaded links, unavailable transforms, unavailable element representative points, missing vertical extents, and boundary-only evidence fail closed instead of becoming Room assignments.

Use spatialKindPreference=room when the user explicitly asks for room numbers. Linked architectural Rooms retain link instance, source document, source-scoped id, phase, containment method, and ambiguity. Same-phase spatial ids remain distinct even when their labels match; only one-per-phase variants with valid lifecycle mapping and one stable numbered identity may collapse across phases.
superComponentId/topLevelParentId/isNested identify nested FamilyInstance records so child geometry is not silently counted as another physical device.

tools.title: Get Placement Context
tools.description: Return host-aware placement diagnostics for one element, including insertion point, type/family, orientation/flip state, exact serializable host-face and linked-element evidence when Revit exposes it, wall-host projection, requested room-side wall context, ranked nearby hosts, circuit membership, and read-only electrical distribution-system evidence for electrical equipment. Body: {elementId,hostCategories?,hostSearchRadiusFt?,maxNearbyHosts?,pointXyz?,roomNumber?,roomSide?}.

tools.title: Create MEP Route
tools.description: Create a multi-segment duct, pipe, or electrical conduit route from ordered XYZ or frame-linked points with dry-run, conservative size/elevation fallbacks, explicit user-workset assignment, internal connector attempts, optional fail-closed endpoint joining, and native readback. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId for required ends; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Duplicate duct/pipe/conduit type names fail closed; use ductTypeId, pipeTypeId, or conduitTypeId for stable native selection. Duct profiles and dimensions must be valid and compatible before starting a transaction. Native route size, duct shape, and requested workset readback must match when verify=true. Use dryRun:false for authorized creation and true for a requested preview. Body: {kind:duct|pipe|conduit,frameId?,points:[{x?,y?,z?,xPx?,yPx?,xyz?}],viewId?,roomNumber?,levelName?,levelId?,worksetName?,worksetId?,systemType?,ductType?,ductTypeId?,ductShape?:round|rectangular|oval,pipeType?,pipeTypeId?,conduitType?,conduitTypeId?,ductSize?,diameter?,pipeSize?,segmentSizes?:string[],sizePolicy?:explicit_required|use_default_with_warning,elevationPolicy?:explicit_required|resolve_context_default,routingMode?:orthogonal|polyline,connectSegments?,connectToExisting?,requireExistingEndpointConnections?,requiredExistingEndpoint?:start|end|both,expectedExistingStartOwnerId?,expectedExistingEndOwnerId?,externalConnectionToleranceFt?,verify?,dryRun?}.
tools.example: dry-run a native conduit, pipe, or duct route with three ordered points
notes: A separate preview is optional. When the user has authorized drafting, use dryRun:false to apply directly; honor any explicit read-only or dry-run request. Native authorization, validation, transaction rollback, and connector verification still apply. If size is omitted, default policy uses 8x8 duct or 1 inch pipe and returns a warning.
Use segmentSizes with one size per segment to draft multi-section routes; internal joints with differing adjacent sizes expect transition fittings.
Internal route joints attempt Revit NewTransitionFitting for size changes, otherwise NewElbowFitting, then fall back to Connector.ConnectTo; fitting ids are returned when created.
Connector verification is conservative: created standalone routes normally report open endpoint connectors until connected to equipment or existing runs.

Only points is universally required. For kind=duct use ductType or ductTypeId plus ductSize/diameter; for kind=pipe use pipeType or pipeTypeId plus pipeSize/diameter; for kind=conduit use conduitType or conduitTypeId plus diameter. These alternatives are not simultaneous requirements.

tools.title: Connect Existing MEP Branch
tools.description: Explicit connectionMode=replace_tee_with_takeoff atomically replaces one connected round duct tee with a straight bridge and native takeoff while retaining both old main ducts and the rigid/flex branch. It requires kind=duct, teeElementId, mainElementId, secondMainElementId, branchElementId, expectedTakeoffTypeId and verify=true; optional branchConnectorId/expectedBranchOriginXyz guard exact identity. Workset is inherited from the main. dryRun=true performs the native operation then rolls the entire group back; dryRun=false applies. Dependent annotation deletion, unexpected created/deleted elements, mismatched main data or changed far connections cause rollback. This mode requires replacement-specific independent absence/network readback before completion; the addition-only graph proof is insufficient. Connect one retained branch to the interior of an existing rigid main without replacing accepted geometry. connectionMode:takeoff_fitting creates a native takeoff between one exact open rigid/flex duct or pipe connector and its main, accepts an explicit worksetId/worksetName, and otherwise inherits the retained branch user workset with committed readback. connectionMode:air_terminal_on_duct uses Revit's direct air-terminal attachment operation, requires kind:duct plus an exact open air-terminal connector, and produces the native direct terminal-to-duct topology without an adapter curve. Both modes guard the active model and projected interior point, preserve pre-existing physical connections, verify the result after transaction commit, and perform the real operation inside a rollback-verified transaction group during dry-run. Each stage runs first with dryRun:true and then once with dryRun:false. Later stages pass hash-ledgered priorActionOutputs so accepted native IDs are never replayed. Each call has its own rollback boundary. Responses echo stageKey and persist created_element_ids, affected_element_ids, and route endpoint IDs; the host ledger binds planned continuation endpoints to those IDs and audits their native connectors before acceptance. In addition to route, family, connection, tag, and circuit creation, the wrapper supports repair-first move, rotate, MEP size/elevation edit, and exact connector repair operations against useful existing elements. Body: {stageKey?,priorActionOutputs?:[{action_key,created_element_ids,affected_element_ids?,route_segment_element_ids?,route_start_element_ids?,route_end_element_ids?,split_main_start_element_ids?,split_main_end_element_ids?}],operations:[{action_key,path,depends_on?,apply_body?,deferred_body?,execution_mode?,provisional_batch_key?,continuation_endpoints?}],dryRun?,verify?,maximumCreatedElements?,targetViewId?,applyTargetViewPhase?,requireAllCreatedElementsVisibleInTargetView?}.

tools.description: One-call duct, pipe, or native conduit route workflow that enforces resolve context -> dry-run -> optional apply -> focused post-change highlight/export. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Plus {apply?:boolean,visualVerify?:boolean,visualViewId?,imageSize?,focusPaddingFt?}. tools.title: MEP Branch Network Workflow

Apply creates the main route first, then connects each branch to its requested main segment using /revit/connect-mep-branch; duct tap/takeoff, pipe tap/takeoff with an explicit Revit takeoff/tap routing preference, retained two-connector transition/reducer anchors, and duct/pipe split tee use the lower-level verified guards. A branch with existingBranchAnchorElementId must use connectionMode:"tee" and never falls back to an open-main or tap path. Accessory graph apply supports explicit duct/pipe accessory insertions hosted on created main or branch segments when a compatible loaded or workspace-scoped familyPath symbol resolves, plus explicit target-id duct/pipe accessory delete and type_change with compatible loaded types. notes: This workflow drafts a main route plus multiple branch connections by composing /revit/create-mep-route and /revit/connect-mep-branch.
Dry-run plans branch projections and branch-level reducer/transition joint plans against the requested main segment geometry before any model write.
Use branches[*].branchSegmentSizes with one size per branch segment; networkPlan.branches[*].jointPlan reports transition expectations before apply.

Apply creates the main, branches, and accessories inside one TransactionGroup. Any branch, accessory, or semantic-verification failure rolls back the complete network; success reports atomicCommitSucceeded=true.

Accessory graph nodes are accepted in the request and surfaced in networkPlan. Apply supports duct/pipe accessory insertion hosted on a created main or branch segment with a compatible resolved family symbol and chainageFt/point, optionally loading an explicit workspace-scoped familyPath first, plus explicit target-id duct/pipe accessory delete and type_change with a compatible loaded type.

Accessory delete/type_change must provide targetElementId or targetElementIds. Type changes also require typeId, targetTypeName, familySymbolId, or familyName/typeName. Inserted accessories must match the route kind category.

tools.title: Reroute MEP Route Segment
tools.description: Guarded edit workflow for one straight duct/pipe curve. Discover candidates with /revit/find-elements includeGeometry:true and screen routeCurveCandidates before trial calls. A size-transition host must be at least 1.0 ft long so the transition can remain 0.5 ft from both ends. Current endpoint preservation requires exactly two physical End connectors and no side/tap Curve connectors; skip tapped hosts instead of weakening connection checks. Set operation:"offset" or operation:"size_transition" explicitly whenever size metadata is also supplied; omitted/auto preserves legacy inference. Offset mode derives two split points from host curve chainage or normalized chainage, reports replacement segments, offset points, selected type/system/level/size, and expected elbow fittings; offsetMode:"dogleg45" uses diagonal setback legs instead of perpendicular legs. Size-transition mode derives one transition point, reports upstream/downstream segment points, explicit selected sizes, and expected transition fitting. Apply replaces the host only after required fittings/connectors succeed, reports created segment/fitting ids, connector/system audit, endpointReconnectionPlan when applicable, and optional trace-enabled focused capture. Connected host endpoints are blocked by default; set preserveConnectedEndpoints:true only after dry-run reports a resolvable start/end endpointReconnectionPlan to reconnect the replacement route to original external endpoint connectors. Mutation flags are canonical: preview requires apply:false,dryRun:true; write requires apply:true,dryRun:false; omitted or equal pairs are rejected. Body size-transition: {operation:size_transition,kind:duct|pipe,hostElementId,transitionChainageFt?|transitionNormalized?,upstreamDuctSize?|downstreamDuctSize?|upstreamDiameter?|downstreamDiameter?|upstreamPipeSize?|downstreamPipeSize?,sizePolicy?,preserveConnectedEndpoints?,apply,dryRun,verify?,visualVerify?,visualViewId?,focusPaddingFt?}.

tools.title: Schedules
tools.description: List native schedules with kind=regular(default)|panel|all and bounded offset/max. Inventory reports exact IDs/UIDs, panel ownership, matched/returned/complete/hasMore/nextOffset; panel templates are excluded. For compact electrical discovery use action=circuits, max=1..500 (default200), offset and optional native panel scheduleId. Without scheduleId it enumerates all project power circuits, including explicit Spare/Space types, and returns both Load Name and Schedule Circuit Notes, native rating/voltage/VA/phase currents, conductor counts, member IDs and model wire profiles. Follow nextOffset for pages; completeness is enumeration, not suitability or verified work. Load classifications do not establish continuous duty; inspect equipment/use and applicable rules. Read panel detail separately for actual visible cell bindings. Only an unfiltered complete inventory establishes whole-project scope. Inspect one regular/panel schedule by native ID. Panel detail by scheduleId with includeData=true returns bounded Header/Body/Summary/Footer visible text, native circuit mapping, cell parameter bindings and circuit editability. Follow per-section row/column continuation; 1..200 rows, 1..40 columns, at most2000cells per section. Panel templates/schedulable fields are excluded. Stored text is not rendered legibility or design verification. For native appearance of a regular or panel schedule INSTANCE, use action:cell_styles, scheduleId and cells:[{section:Header|Body|Summary|Footer,row,column}], 1..64 absolute native locators. Returns exact text, grid/sheet RGB, override/merged-range state and complete table-content/unrequested-style hashes. Use merged top-left locators and action:list,kind:panel to resolve panel schedule IDs. Both Load Name and Schedule Circuit Notes can carry compact wiring notation; description-only coverage is incomplete. These cell reads are separate from regular field/detail metadata. Detail accepts includeSchedulableFields, schedulableFieldOffset, maxSchedulableFields (1..200) for exact native eligible column names, parameter IDs and field types with total/nextOffset; follow every page before claiming absence. For independent clone-definition checking, opt in to includeDefinitionSnapshot:true on action:detail with an exact scheduleId, fields enabled and no query. This bounded flat-definition reader includes combined constituents, native field formats, filters/sort/phasing and deduplicated cell styles; incomplete/unsupported calculated or embedded definitions are explicit, and ordinary reads omit this larger snapshot. For separate native default-style/order verification use {action:presentation,scheduleId}. It returns requested schedule defaults, bounded unchanged-content/style/geometry fingerprints of other regular schedules and native logical dependencies, with explicit incomplete/error state. These reads prove declared native values/preservation coverage, not rendered legibility or engineering. Detail returns authoritative field metadata, filter definitions, appearance/settings readback, and optional bounded visible header/body cell reads with includeData, rowOffset, columnOffset, maxRows, and maxColumns. Set requireUniqueQuery=true for natural-name detail lookup to return explicit NotFound/Ambiguous candidates instead of silently selecting the first substring match.

The file is opened temporarily and closed without saving; no editable session, load, placement, type selection or save is exposed. Source path/hash and native family parameter storageType/specTypeId/unitTypeId/currentValue are returned; unsupported metadata stays explicit. External-file facts are not loaded-project verification and do not establish design suitability. A type is inspected directly without creating an instance; this read does not broaden family-edit source authority. A tag resolves its own annotation family, not the tagged equipment. Empty driverParameters does not prove an unbound label; unboundLabelCount is null whenever label rows are returned. driverParameterObservation distinguishes references_observed, binding_undetermined, not_requested and read_error; none proves complete binding or compatibility. Counts concern returned label rows only. parameterDrivenLabelCount is a legacy alias counting observed driver references, not verified label binding. Linked-model category override requests block with linked_model_category_override_not_supported rather than changing host categories. set_crop_box supports annotationCropActive and annotationCropMarginFeet for tight sheet viewport extents. Supports linePatternId|linePatternName in category/filter overrides, and create_view_filter rule fields {ruleParameterName,ruleOperator,ruleValue,ruleCaseSensitive}.

Require complete:true, equal categoryIdsSha256/count and otherCategoriesSha256, then compare target attributes; unsupported/failed reads remain unverified. Reuses owned views, atomically replaces only unchanged owned notes, retains unused continuation views. Whole records are paged within64KiB; follow nextOffset with the returned expectedSourceSha256. Changed files return SourceChanged with no continuation records. Formula errors/missing cached results stay explicit; never recalculates or silently zeros them. Layout/rich-style source retained separately from raw cached cell text; not formatted Excel display or native import/visual proof. Does not expose the legacy Excel mutation as supported.

Exact existing drafting view scale and UniqueId are required; no view or scale is silently changed. Inspect every committed part with inspect-vector-detail for native source projection and integral original-PDF reparse, then continue using fresh snapshot. Already-created parts are not duplicated; uncertain writes must not be retried. Source omissions, visual comparison, complete drawing coverage and save/reopen are separate. dryRun is plan-only.

tools.title: Inspect Imported Vector Detail
tools.description: action=list discovers managed vector details without model changes. Otherwise exact manifestElementId returns source/view context and fresh native ownership snapshot for continuation. Add partIndex for a complete native geometry/text/style source-projection check of that part. includeItems=true pages whole native records with offset/limit; default summary avoids flooding context. Missing/changed native content stays explicit and blocks blind continuation. The integral backend independently re-extracts the original registered PDF for source verification. Native/source checks are separate from visual comparison, sheet fit and saved-reopen qualification. Reattach an older source PDF if it is absent from this conversation.
tools.example: inspect every imported vector part against the source and obtain the fresh continuation snapshot

tools.title: Import Editable Excel Output Table
tools.description: Inspect the original .xlsx and choose its actual output sheetName first. Import source-bound editable native text and borders into readable continuation drafting views; no200row truncation or whole-sheet shrink. Require sourcePath, sheetName, expectedSourceSha256 and viewName. layout uses printed inches, minimumTextPoints and optional exact range/repeatHeaderRows. Border weights map hair/thin/medium/thick to explicit Revit1-16 weights, defaults1/1/3/5. Each call commits one complete part in source order. Continue ALL remaining parts with returned partIndex plus exact manifestElementId and fresh expectedImportSnapshotSha256 from inspect-excel-import. Existing parts are never duplicated; changed source/layout/native content refuses continuation. Errors remain literal; no recalculation or engineering approval. Unsupported formatting fails explicitly. Inspect each part, place all views on sheets and review actual work-area visuals separately. dryRun is not an executed preview.
tools.example: add the ventilation output table, continue every readable part and verify it before sheet placement

tools.title: Inspect Imported Excel Table Parts
tools.description: action=list discovers owned Excel imports. Otherwise sourcePath and manifestElementId inspect the whole retained source projection and fresh root snapshot for continuation. Add exact partIndex for complete native text/format/cell-bound/order/border checks of THAT part. section=notes|cells|borders|issues pages whole records; follow nextOffset with expectedInspectionSnapshotSha256. Summary has no per-part native verification unless partIndex is supplied. Missing/changed source, native content, ownership and stale cursors remain explicit. This is not visual fidelity, sheet-fit, recalculation or engineering proof. Use actual model-area visuals and saved-reopen checks separately.

tools.title: Export Elements to Excel Workbook (.xlsx)
tools.description: Export selected elements to an Excel spreadsheet under Workspace without changing Revit. Native typed values, units, display and field status in Elements, Issues and Readme. Use observed elementIds and exact parameterNames (max 2000 elements, 100 fields); inspect a representative element first. Optional supplementalTables preserve supplied inputs, proposed device quantities and review results, visibly assistant-authored with native identity columns. Each table requires every selected elementId exactly once; missing, duplicate or foreign rows reject before writing. Up to 4 tables, 32 columns each, 64000 total cells; scalar JSON values only (null is missing, zero remains zero, strings are not formulas). Body: {elementIds:[...],parameterNames:[...],outputFolder?,fileName?,dryRun?,supplementalTables:[{name,contentKind:'user_input_transcription'|'assistant_proposal'|'review',columns:[...],rows:[{elementId,values:[...]}]}]}. Supply all requested spaces and deliverables; native selection coverage is not proof of complete task scope or engineering correctness. Existing files are never overwritten. Verify artifact_receipt with inspect-exported-files.

outputFolder.description: Prefer omitting this field: the default is artifacts/xlsx inside the Operator workspace. A supplied folder must be under that workspace; a relative folder is recommended. Documents, Downloads and other external folders are rejected before writing.

fileName.description: Simple unique workbook name, without directories. Existing destinations are never overwritten.

supplementalTables.description: Every table, including review, must contain each selected elementId exactly once. Include a review row even for an element with no issues; put general notes into those rows instead of adding duplicate element rows. Each row has one scalar value per column. Preserve explicit zero versus unknown null. Values are assistant-authored, not native or verified engineering facts. Across all tables: at most 64000 cells and 1000000 text characters.

tools.title: Tag Elements
tools.description: Create tags for elements by explicit ids and/or category selectors in a target view, with duplicate avoidance for IndependentTag, local RoomTag and local SpaceTag associations. Native room and space tags retain their model-backed name/number; a static TextNote is not an associative tag. Local Rooms/Spaces can be discovered across the document even when their category is hidden in the target view. Linked room IDs are not host element IDs; do not substitute an unrelated local subject or claim linked-room tagging support. Check the actual local subject before creating a spatial tag, with duplicate avoidance, optional per-category tag-type mapping, and additive geometry-aware placement/readback. geometry_aware uses the same category resolution for visibility and loaded/source family selection, including OST_DuctCurves -> OST_DuctTags and the existing equipment/fixture categories; mixed or unsupported target categories remain unresolved. geometry_aware places tag heads outside target footprints, avoids annotation/target/tag collisions, prefers clear plan space over walls and modeled equipment, keeps leaders bounded, rejects leader crossings and protected-content routes, uses discipline profiles, and requires actual Revit tag and leader geometry before retaining created work. Keep creation and existing-tag repair fields separate: addLeader is for creation (default false in offset mode, true in geometry_aware); hasLeader and exact coordinates require repairExistingTagId. Mixed-mode fields are rejected before mutation. Existing tags can be read or repaired in place with repairExistingTagId plus exact tag-head/free-leader coordinates; dry runs execute the native tag repair, read it back, roll it back, and verify the original tag geometry. If no compatible tag is loaded, autoLoadTagFamily can import an exactly category-compatible tag from a workspace-scoped source project, optionally selecting an exact source family/type; dry-run reports bounded source candidates. generatedTagContentProfile=airflow_only produces a copied source family that retains bounded flow-unit labels and removes unrelated text/label content, with an explicit sanitization receipt. A dry-run may set inspectTagFamilyElements=true to return a bounded read-only inventory of the selected tag family's internal elements and parameters. Tags with no visible/measurable head geometry or no professionally clear tag/leader route are removed and reported as failures. Create body: {viewId?|viewName?,elementIds?|categoryNames?,categoryTagTypeMap?,tagTypeId?|tagTypeName?|tagFamilyName?,onlyUntagged?,addLeader?,orientation?:horizontal|vertical,offsetX?,offsetY?,placementMode?:offset|geometry_aware,placementProfile?:auto|mep|electrical|architectural,tagWidthPaperInches?,tagHeightPaperInches?,clearancePaperInches?,maxRepairAttempts?,autoLoadTagFamily?,tagFamilySourceProjectPath?,tagFamilySourceCategory?,tagFamilySourceFamilyName?,tagFamilySourceTypeName?,generatedTagFamilyName?,generatedTagContentProfile?:none|airflow_only,inspectTagFamilyElements?,max?,dryRun?}. Existing-tag body: {viewId?|viewName?,repairExistingTagId,tagHeadPositionXyz?,leaderEndXyz?,leaderElbowXyz?,hasLeader?,leaderEndCondition?:attached|free,dryRun?}.

Use a drafting view at viewScale:1 for paper-size CAD details. importUnit controls source geometry units. customScale overrides importUnit; customScale:1 alone is not proof of one-to-one printed size. Verify actual native transform and sheet output.
cadCategories returns native imported layer identities for scoped view graphics overrides. A whole-link lineweight override is not a substitute for changing only the requested new-work layers.

tools.title: Configure Schedule
tools.description: To combine existing parameter columns on a regular schedule, send only {scheduleId,combinedField:{name,sourceFieldIds,index?,separator?,hideSourceFields?,widthFeet?},dryRun?}. sourceFieldIds are native schedule-field IDs from detail.fields, NOT model ElementIds. Creates a genuine combined parameter field, preserves parameter values and source fields (hidden by default), refuses name collisions, and returns native definition and change inventory. Separate host presentation read verifies ordered bindings, headings, widths and preservation; inspect enlarged rendering for visual quality. For a background-only edit on a regular or panel schedule INSTANCE, use {scheduleId,cellStyles:[{section,row,column,expectedText,backgroundColorRgb:[r,g,b]}],dryRun?:false}. Copies existing style and preserves table text/notes, unrequested cells and other formatting. expectedText must match a native read exactly. 1..64 cells; no mixing other operations/shared-template edits/text or parameter writes. After commit independently read /revit/schedules action:cell_styles for ALL targets and inspect rendering; native color checks do not certify the visual result. Filters use {field|fieldId,op,value?,valueType?}; valueType is string (default), element_id, integer, double (Revit internal units), or display (field/document units). Resolve element IDs from current document evidence. Filter replacement is atomic; ambiguous field names require fieldId. Except for cellStyles above, advanced configuration requires a regular ViewSchedule; PanelScheduleView row heights and literal text use native API operations (TableSectionData.SetRowHeight/SetCellText), followed by exact native getters and a visual check. Native title/header/body styles: appearance.titleTextTypeId/headerTextTypeId/bodyTextTypeId select existing TextNoteTypes without editing shared styles. Read /revit/schedules detail presentation for current style IDs, font/size and override caveats. fieldOrder is an exact permutation of ALL native field IDs (including hidden), obtained from detail.fields; add fields first then reorder separately. z.description: Feet; absolute model elevation in absolute_model mode, native level offset in ordinary legacy mode.
